discussion_comments.comment_body: deep equal because practically all shaders were passing a different `uniformsProp` identity when re-rendered (`memo` we are using helped but not in all cases)
this is super cute 😂 I think stephen had a similar comment, but would love to see an explicit branch to turn off speed so it's immediately obvious what's happening when document visible is false
What's the advantage to this? Are you thinking just avoiding the microtask queue or is there something else?

Which in particular, it being conditionally async, or this line in particular?

If conditionally async: well yeah make it synchronous if there isn't any async work. And if there's complexity to be added it's definitely here instead of userland

If this line in particular: it's because the function isn't async anymore so I need to use promises directly

> make it synchronous if there isn't any async work

Yeah, my question is about this part ^^^. What's the advantage of this?

at this point it's a microoptimization, mostly agreed, but I would argue it aids in the initial rendering of the shader when there are no images present, and when we made the change to take images it could have been seen as a performance regression?

Lord knows I could be wrong, but I'm not aware of any meaningful cost for a single `async` function call. It should be in the single digit microseconds. Sometimes if there are thousands of them they can add up, but I think this just happens once per uniforms change.

A simpler, consistent internal API and less code in general seems better.

alright removing the code 😁 — I couldn't find any visible difference between the two implementations on the paper docs site, if it smells like it could be delaying things later I'll come back to this (e.g. vlad was mentioning paper shaders being delayed a frame when dragging onto the canvas, was hoping this might be it but maybe not)
